title: Will and Confession
premise: Silas Eriksen, the coroner of the fading town of Halloway Bend, is paid a retainer by a dying woman named Vera Ashcombe to prove that her brother's disappearance thirty years ago was NOT a murder — a strange request that unravels into something darker: the brother is alive, hiding in plain sight, and Vera wants Silas to find him before her death triggers an inheritance clause that will expose and destroy him. As Silas digs through old alibis, she discovers the town's founding families conspired to fake a death to protect him from a crime he didn't commit, and that her own late father helped bury the truth. When Vera dies and her heirs move to claim the estate, Silas must choose between the law she serves and the found family she never expected, exposing the conspiracy at the town's centennial gathering — and claiming her place in a family that chose her back.
about_author: B. M. Thornbury is the pen name of a former rural records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing unsolved disappearances across three counties. They write quiet mysteries about the weight small towns carry, and this is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Silas Eriksen's POV. A frail stranger, Vera Ashcombe, arrives at the coroner's office with a cash retainer and an impossible request: prove her brother Edwin's death thirty years ago never happened. Silas, who prides herself on closable cases, is unsettled by the phrasing 'yet' in Vera's warning. The beat is intrigue laced with professional pride wounded by mystery.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas walks the cemetery at dawn, confirming Edwin Ashcombe's headstone and the absence of any body in county records. Her assistant, Dee, a runaway Silas informally adopted, pushes back on taking the case. Flashback hints at Silas's father, the previous coroner. The beat is loneliness softened by found-family warmth.

chapters.title: Alibis in Amber
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera recalls the night of Edwin's disappearance in 1994: four families, one bonfire, and a pact sworn on the Ashcombe porch. She reveals the inheritance clause — her will will trigger a public inquest unless Edwin is found alive first. The beat is guilt curdling into desperation.

chapters.title: The Four Families
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas interviews the pact's surviving members: matriarch Odette Crane, retired sheriff Hollis Vann, and pharmacist Bram Tully. Each gives a flawless alibi — too flawless, word-for-word identical after thirty years. The beat is creeping unease as rehearsed lies surface.

chapters.title: Dee's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Dee, digging through county archives for fun, finds a 1994 coroner's report signed by Silas's father — ruling Edwin dead without a body. She hides it, torn between loyalty and truth. The beat is the first crack in Silas's idealized memory of her father.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas searches the riverbank where Edwin was 'drowned' and finds a rotted satchel containing a man's watch, still ticking — recently wound. Someone visits the river. The beat is dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Odette's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. Odette, the pact's architect, nearly tells Silas everything but stops when her grandson enters. She reveals only that Edwin 'did something noble and terrible' and that protecting him was the town's penance. The beat is loyalty at war with conscience.

chapters.title: The Heir Arrives
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Vera's estranged son, Marcus Ashcombe, sweeps into town with a lawyer, eager for his mother to die and the estate to settle. He pressures Silas to drop the case. The beat is open hostility — the antagonist steps forward.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Sundays
chapters.summary: Hollis Vann's POV. The retired sheriff confesses to Silas that he falsified the drowning report under pressure from Silas's own father, who believed Edwin was protecting someone. Hollis doesn't say who. The beat is betrayal — Silas learns her father was complicit.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Dee finds a 1994 photo in the archives: Edwin alive at a bus depot, three days after his 'death,' with a woman whose face is scratched out. She finally shows Silas, breaking her silence. The beat is trust deepening — the found family chooses honesty.

chapters.title: Vera Fails
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera suffers a stroke, leaving her unable to speak clearly. Marcus gains power of attorney and moves to revoke Silas's retainer. Silas realizes the clock is now measured in Vera's heartbeats. The beat is urgency — time is running out, literally.

chapters.title: Bram's Pharmacy Window
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas notices Bram Tully refilling a prescription monthly for a man named 'E. Ash' at an address that doesn't exist. Following the delivery route, she reaches an abandoned orchard cabin with fresh smoke in the stovepipe. The beat is the hunt tightening.

chapters.title: The Man in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Edwin's POV. Edwin Ashcombe, alive and old, watches Silas approach and prepares to run. Instead she sits on his step and waits. He tells her he faked his death to shield someone — and that the person he shielded was Vera herself. The beat is revelation and reluctant trust.

chapters.title: What Edwin Saw
chapters.summary: Edwin's POV. Edwin recounts the bonfire night: he caught Vera's husband, Richard, attempting to poison Vera for her inheritance, and in the struggle Richard died. The four families buried the truth to protect Vera, who was pregnant with Marcus. The beat is the full picture assembling — love against duty.

chapters.title: Marcus's Ledger
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas discovers Marcus has known Edwin was alive for years — and has been blackmailing him, extracting money in exchange for silence, planning to expose him the moment the estate settles to invalidate Vera's will. The beat is the true villain unmasked.

chapters.title: Dee, Interrogated
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus, realizing Silas is close, threatens Dee with her juvenile record and an old warrant to force her to report Silas's findings. Dee pretends to comply. The beat is menace — the antagonist closes in, and the found family is targeted.

chapters.title: Vera's Last Word
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Vera, briefly lucid, scrawls a note to Silas: 'Tell him I never stopped setting two plates.' She asks Silas to bring Edwin to her, law be damned. The beat is heartbreak — love against duty made personal.

chapters.title: The Centennial Gathering
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At Halloway Bend's centennial, Marcus announces the estate settlement and plans to 'honor' his uncle's memory — a trap to force Edwin's exposure. Silas, Dee, Odette, and Hollis converge. The beat is rising tension at its peak.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas takes the stage and confesses everything — Richard's death, the pact, her father's cover-up, Marcus's blackmail — presenting the watch, the photograph, and the pharmacy ledger. Edwin walks into the crowd, alive. The beat is the climax: truth as an act of love.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: Hollis and Odette's POVs. The fallout: Marcus is arrested for blackmail and evidence tampering; the state declines to prosecute Edwin given Richard's attempted murder and the decades served in exile. Odette publicly takes responsibility for the pact. The beat is justice, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Two Plates
chapters.summary: Edwin's POV. Edwin, freed, sits at Vera's bedside for the supper she waited thirty years for. She dies that night, at peace, her hand in her brother's. Silas stands witness outside the door. The beat is grief braided with completion — love outlasting duty.

chapters.title: Will and Confession
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, epilogue. Vera's will is read: she leaves Silas the orchard cabin and a letter calling her 'the daughter the town forgot to give me.' Dee officially moves in; Edwin tends the graves, including a new stone for Vera. Silas, who knows every grave by name, finally feels known by one. The beat is resolution — found family, inherited by choice.
